article.description: El hielo cerca de la cumbre del pico montañoso indonesio se ha reducido a parches dispersos demasiado pequeños para fluir como glaciares.
article.explanation:
**El último hielo en el Puncak Jaya**

El Puncak Jaya, ubicado en la cordillera Sudirman de Indonesia, ha sido uno de los pocos lugares cerca del ecuador donde el hielo ha persistido durante todo el año. Sin embargo, las imágenes satelitales muestran una alarmante reducción de sus glaciares. En 1988, estos cubrían aproximadamente 4.31 kilómetros cuadrados, mientras que para septiembre de 2025, solo quedaban alrededor de 0.09 kilómetros cuadrados, lo que representa cerca del 2% de su extensión original.

El espesor del hielo también ha disminuido drásticamente. En 2010, el hielo en el sitio de monitoreo principal tenía una altura de 32 metros, pero para 2023, este se redujo a solo 4 metros. Este proceso de adelgazamiento ha llevado a que los glaciares se fragmenten, creando bordes expuestos que aceleran el derretimiento.

Los científicos advierten que, debido a las condiciones climáticas actuales y fenómenos como El Niño, la desaparición total de estos glaciares podría ocurrir alrededor de 2030. Durante eventos de El Niño pasados, el hielo se ha derretido a un ritmo alarmante, lo que subraya la vulnerabilidad de estas masas de hielo en un clima cambiante.

Only a few small fragments of ice remain, shown in blue, and bare brown rock covers most of the ridgetops that were icy in 1988. NASA Earth Observatory / Lauren Dauphin A false-color satellite image shows the same area in 2026. Only a few small fragments of ice remain, shown in blue, and bare brown rock covers most of the ridgetops that were icy in 1988. NASA Earth Observatory / Lauren Dauphin 1988 2026 Curtain Toggle 2-Up On the island of New Guinea, Indonesia’s Sudirman Range is one of the few places near the equator that have long held ice year-round. But near the summit of Puncak Jaya, the ice has dwindled to patches too small to flow like glaciers. Positioned in the tropics beside the largest expanse of warm ocean water on Earth, the range’s glaciers lie near the warmest conditions in which ice can survive year-round. Scientists have described these glaciers as high-altitude “ canaries in the coal mine ,” alongside other tropical ice such as the remnants of Humboldt Glacier in Venezuela, Quelccaya Ice Cap in Peru, and the ice fields of Kilimanjaro in Tanzania. The change on Puncak Jaya is visible in this image pair, acquired in 1988 by the TM (Thematic Mapper) on Landsat 5 (left) and in 2026 by the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 (right). The false-color images help distinguish areas of ice (light blue) from exposed bedrock (brown). Clouds appear white and vegetation green. In 1988, the glaciers covered about 4.31 square kilometers (1.66 square miles), according to Donaldi Permana, a climate scientist at the Indonesian Agency for Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics ( BMKG ). By September 2025, satellite and aerial data showed that only about 0.09 square kilometers (0.03 square miles) remained—an area equivalent to about a dozen soccer fields. That’s roughly 2 percent of the 1988 extent . An aerial survey planned for December should yield an estimate of how much ice remains in 2026, Permana said. The glaciers have thinned, too. Measurements at the primary monitoring site on the East Northwall Firn showed a drop from 32 meters (105 feet) thick in 2010 to 4 meters (13 feet) in 2023, Permana said. By November 2024, the ice at this site was gone. As the glaciers thin, they also break apart, and each new fragment adds exposed edges where ice can melt, compounding the losses. In the 2026 Landsat image, freshly uncovered bedrock appears between the remnants. Snow still falls in the area, but it doesn’t last long enough on the bare rock to build up into new ice. “It’s a house of cards problem,” said Chris Shuman, a retired University of Maryland glaciologist who has tracked Puncak Jaya’s glaciers in satellite imagery. “Once this process gets going, there’s really no turning back.” To qualify as a glacier, a body of ice generally has to be thick enough to flow downhill under its own weight, and it needs an area where snow builds up faster than it melts. Puncak Jaya’s remaining ice has thinned so much and broken into such small, stagnant patches that it no longer flows. “While small ice remnants persist in high-altitude crevices around Puncak Jaya, their functional life as active glaciers is effectively over,” Permana said. As for the remaining patches of ice, time will tell how long they last. Recent satellite studies suggest complete disappearance of the main glacial ice areas could occur around 2030. Permana noted that BMKG estimates suggest they could be gone much sooner, hastened by the current El Niño . Past El Niño years have hit these glaciers especially hard. As the air warms, the freezing level rises above the summit, so precipitation falls as rain instead of snow. That means less fresh white snow that normally reflects sunlight and shields the ice, leaving darker surfaces that absorb more heat and melt faster. During the 2015-2016 El Niño, the ice thinned about five times faster than usual , losing roughly 5.3 meters (17 feet) of thickness in a single year. The 2023-2024 El Niño brought another bout of rapid thinning, about 2 to 4 meters (7 to 13 feet) per year. article.explanation:
**Nuevo álbum de sonidos de estrellas bebés compartido por el Chandra de la NASA**

El Observatorio de Rayos X Chandra de la NASA ha lanzado un nuevo álbum que transforma datos de estrellas en formación en sonidos. Este proyecto incluye cuatro nuevas sonificaciones que permiten a los astrónomos estudiar mejor el ciclo de vida de las estrellas, incluyendo nuestro propio Sol.

Uno de los lugares destacados es la galaxia Messier 82, conocida como una galaxia de "explosión estelar", donde se forman estrellas a un ritmo mucho más alto que en la Vía Láctea. Chandra ha capturado plumas de gas caliente generadas por estrellas jóvenes que explotan rápidamente.

Otro foco es la Nebulosa de Orión, un área cercana a la Tierra con más de mil estrellas activas. En la sonificación de estos datos, las estrellas emiten sonidos brillantes, mientras que la emisión difusa de rayos X se traduce en tonos altos.

La Nebulosa de Carina, famosa por sus "Acantilados Cósmicos", también se incluye en el álbum. Aquí, Chandra detecta estrellas bebés que producen sonidos cortos, mientras que la radiación X se convierte en notas más largas.

Estos avances no solo enriquecen nuestra comprensión del cosmos, sino que también ofrecen una nueva forma de experimentar el universo.

article.source_body: 4 Min Read New Album of Baby Star Sounds Shared by NASA’s Chandra A new album from NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory collects snapshots of baby stars across the galaxy and beyond and transforms that data into sound. Four new sonifications use data of stars that are actively forming, captured by Chandra and other NASA telescopes By studying places in the universe where stars are currently being born and young stars are present, astronomers can better understand the lifecycle of all stars, including our own Sun. NASA/CXC/SAO/K.Arcand, SYSTEM Sounds (M. Russo, A. Santaguida M82 The galaxy Messier 82 (M82) is called a starburst galaxy because stars are forming there at a rate tens or even hundreds of times higher than in our Milky Way galaxy. This stellar birth boom may be due to a collision with another galaxy in the past. Today, Chandra sees giant plumes of hot gas that are the byproduct of young, giant stars that quickly explode and other star formation activity. One of the new sonifications combines Chandra’s data with optical data from NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope, as well as infrared views from NASA’s James Webb and retired Spitzer space telescopes. The sonification of the three types of light begins with a radar-like scan that is louder where sources are brighter. The X-ray data is mapped to the highest range of frequencies heard. Infrared data is heard as a low drone plus plucked sounds, while the optical data turns into a range of musical pitches and textures. article.explanation:
**TITULAR: APOD: 17 de noviembre de 2026 – Vía Láctea versus Aurora**

En la imagen del día de hoy, se presenta un fascinante contraste entre la Vía Láctea y una aurora boreal, capturada desde Kvaløya, Noruega. A la izquierda, la Vía Láctea se despliega como un arco central, representando un antiguo sistema de estrellas, gas y polvo que ha existido mucho antes de la formación de la Tierra. Este vasto conjunto de materia se encuentra a distancias inimaginables de nuestro planeta.

Por otro lado, a la derecha, se observa un arco auroral, un fenómeno que se forma en la atmósfera terrestre a partir de átomos y moléculas energizados. Este espectáculo natural es el resultado de partículas energéticas expulsadas por el Sol, que interactúan con el campo magnético de la Tierra. La imagen destaca cómo estos dos gigantes celestiales parecen competir por el dominio del cielo, aunque en realidad se encuentran en diferentes escalas y contextos temporales.

En el fondo de la imagen, se puede identificar la constelación del Gran Carro, y aún más lejos, la galaxia de Andrómeda, lo que añade una capa adicional de profundidad y maravilla a esta representación del cosmos.

article.source_body: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 17 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Original Annotated Milky Way versus Aurora Explanation: Are these two giant arches battling for control of the sky? No, but it sure looks like it! The arch on the left is the central band of our Milky Way Galaxy , an ancient system of stars, gas, and dust that predates our Earth and is very far away. The arch on the right, by contrast, is an auroral ribbon that is only hours old, composed of energized atoms and molecules , and is close by — right in Earth’s upper atmosphere . article.explanation:
**Chipre: Isla de serpientes, gatos y ofiolitas**

Chipre, una isla con una rica historia geológica, comenzó a formarse hace aproximadamente 90 millones de años. Este proceso se debió a la actividad volcánica en el fondo marino, que dio origen a una corteza oceánica que, con el tiempo, emergió gracias a fuerzas tectónicas. Las rocas ofiolitas, que caracterizan la isla, son visibles en las montañas Troodos.

El paisaje de Chipre ha sido moldeado por la sedimentación a lo largo de los años. Durante el Mioceno, se acumularon capas de rocas sedimentarias que contribuyeron a la formación de la península de Akrotiri, unida a la isla principal por dos tombolos. Esta península alberga el lago salado de Akrotiri, que, aunque históricamente ha atraído a grandes poblaciones de flamencos, ha visto una drástica disminución en su número, pasando de 4,000 aves a solo 30 en 2025.

Además, Chipre es famosa por su población de serpientes, especialmente las víboras de nariz plana. En el pasado, la isla fue conocida como Ophiousa, lo que refleja su abundancia de estos reptiles. Para controlar su población, se introdujeron gatos desde Egipto, y hoy en día, se estima que hay tantos gatos como habitantes en la isla, superando el millón.

article.source_body: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Cyprus: Island of Snakes,… Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search Seasonal rains had started to fill Akrotiri Salt Lake when the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 8 captured this image of Cyprus’s Akrotiri Peninsula on October 10, 2026. NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison The island of Cyprus began to form some 90 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous , with molten rock pouring from the seafloor, solidifying, and building new oceanic crust . Over time, portions of this oceanic rock were wrenched upward by tectonic forces , eventually emerging as a rugged island made of ophiolite , a type of rock with a mottled green appearance said to look like the skin of a snake. Remnants of that ancient island are still visible in the dark rocks of the Troodos Mountains . During the Miocene , considerably younger layers of chalk, limestone, marl, and other marine sedimentary rocks accumulated around the island, providing material that developed into a second, smaller island to the south during a later period of geologic uplift . Over time, sediment poured from rivers into the channel separating the two islands and combined with marine sediments to create deltas and eventually two land bridges, or tombolos . The joined landmass comprises the Akrotiri Peninsula , now the southernmost tip of Cyprus. The sandy edges of the peninsula were visible when Landsat 8 captured these images on October 10, 2026. Akrotiri Salt Lake , a coastal lagoon that was once an arm of the Mediterranean Sea, lies between the two tombolos. The more westerly feature, the Kouris River tombolo, formed first, developing about 50,000 years ago from river-deposited gravels and sands. The eastern tombolo extended southward from Cyprus, cutting off the Mediterranean Sea only within the past 2,000 years, according to geologists . The lake’s water levels now vary markedly with the seasons, typically filling in the late autumn and winter and drying out in the summer. The influx of winter water has historically attracted sizable overwintering flamingo populations, averaging about 4,000 birds. However, the wintering flamingo population has declined in recent years, plummeting to 30 birds in 2025, according to news reports . Flamingos have long flocked to the lake to feed on fairy shrimp , which are rich in colorful substances called carotenoids that give the birds their famously pink hue . Snakes are another of the island’s more notorious animal inhabitants. In antiquity, Cyprus was known as Ophiousa , or “ land of snakes ,” likely due to its robust population of blunt-nosed vipers . According to legend, the island’s snake communities grew to be so problematic during a drought in the fourth century that the Roman Empress Helena , mother of Constantine the Great, called for shiploads of cats to be sent from Egypt to control the venomous reptiles. The first feline imports were released in a particularly snake-infested area on the southeastern part of the Akrotiri Peninsula, an area that came to be known as Cape Gata (Cape Cat in Greek). The cape today is still home to the Holy Monastery of St. Nicholas of the Cats , a place where legend says that monks encouraged newly arrived Egyptian cats to hunt snakes. Today, Cyprus has as many cats as people, with more than one million of the feline predators stalking the island. The handful of nuns who now live in the monastery still care for hundreds of cats, according to the St. Nicholas Center . A broader image of Cyprus captured by the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 8 shows the western half of the island on October 10, 2026. article.explanation:
**A la sombra de gigantes volcánicos**

El volcán Tharsis Tholus, ubicado en Marte, ha captado la atención de los científicos gracias a su compleja historia geológica. Con una altura de aproximadamente 8 km, es uno de los volcanes más destacados del planeta rojo, aunque no se compara con los gigantes como Olympus Mons, que alcanza casi 22 km.

Las imágenes recientes de la misión Mars Express revelan características fascinantes de Tharsis Tholus, incluyendo su caldera, una depresión en la cima formada por colapsos tras erupciones. Se han identificado al menos dos colapsos calderales en su historia, lo que sugiere una actividad volcánica significativa en el pasado. Estas calderas son inusualmente grandes en relación con el tamaño del volcán, alcanzando casi 3 km de profundidad.

Además, las laderas del volcán presentan diversas formaciones geológicas, como escarpes y fallas, resultado de la presión ejercida por su masa sobre las capas más blandas del subsuelo. La erosión y los impactos de meteoritos han dejado su huella en la superficie, creando un paisaje complejo y dinámico.

El estudio de Tharsis Tholus no solo enriquece nuestro conocimiento sobre Marte, sino que también ofrece comparaciones valiosas con la actividad volcánica en la Tierra, destacando las diferencias en los procesos geológicos entre ambos planetas.

**NASA Space Apps Challenge bate récords globales de hackatones**

El NASA Space Apps Challenge, celebrado el 14 y 15 de noviembre, ha alcanzado un hito sin precedentes al registrar a 181,835 participantes en 593 eventos alrededor del mundo. Este evento anual invita a los participantes a utilizar los datos abiertos de NASA para abordar uno de los 14 desafíos relacionados con la exploración espacial o la ciencia de la Tierra. Desde su inicio en 2012, el Space Apps Challenge ha reunido a más de 600,000 personas de más de 190 países. La iniciativa no solo ofrece una experiencia práctica con la ciencia de NASA, sino que también moviliza a una comunidad global de tecnólogos y entusiastas del espacio para encontrar soluciones a problemas que afectan a la humanidad.

article.source_body: 2 min read NASA Space Apps Challenge Breaks Global Hackathon Records Two NASA Space Apps Challenge participants in Vilhena, Brazil work together during the annual hackathon on their project submission. NASA On Nov. 14 and 15, NASA held the annual Space Apps Challenge with a record-breaking 181,835 registered participants taking part in 593 events around the world. The annual hackathon invites participants to use NASA’s open data to address one of 14 challenges focused on space exploration or Earth science. This year, the hackathon drew 59% more registrants and was the 5th year in a row with increased participation. Since 2012, NASA Space Apps Challenge has hosted the two-day event, which has included more than 600,000 people from more than 190 countries. The challenge provides an opportunity for hands-on experience with NASA science, mobilizing an engaged global community of technologists and space science enthusiasts to answer questions that benefit humanity and drive exploration. Participants join events organized by local volunteers to work in teams and address one of the challenges and submit their project before the deadline. Projects are then judged to determine 10 global winners, to be announced in January. “The Space Apps Challenge invites people with many different skillsets to leverage NASA’s gold-standard datasets to address real challenges facing us here on Earth and in space,” said Amy Kaminski, engagement branch chief, Science Mission Directorate, NASA Headquarters in Washington. “We’re thrilled to see more than 180,000 people tackling these challenges and helping to accelerate our ability to find solutions.” One of the local winning teams from NASA Space Apps Challenge NYC pose with volunteer local lead Nate Cooper. NASA Challenges also feature data from 17 international space agency partners, all Artemis Accord signatories. This year’s space agency partners are: Angola National Space Programme Management Office (GGPEN), Bahrain Space Agency, Brazilian Space Agency (AEB), CSA (Canadian Space Agency), ESA (European Space Agency), ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation), Italian Space Agency, JAXA (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency), KASA (Korea AeroSpace Administration), Mohammed Bin Rashid Space Center of the United Arab Emirates, National Space Activities Commission of Argentina (CONAE), Nigeria’s National Space Research and Development Agency, Paraguayan Space Agency, Senegalese Space Studies Agency, Spanish Space Agency, Turkish Space Agency, and UK Space Agency. article.explanation:
**NASA Anuncia Premios de Relé Satelital Ka-Band para Comunicaciones Espaciales**

NASA ha seleccionado a tres empresas para desarrollar conceptos de capacidad de relé espacial en banda Ka, compatibles con misiones actuales. Este avance busca asegurar la continuidad del servicio para naves espaciales existentes sin necesidad de modificar sus sistemas a bordo.

Los contratos, bajo el programa Next Space Technologies for Exploration Partnerships-3, son de precio fijo y permiten a NASA financiar el desarrollo desde la fase inicial hasta una demostración de vuelo en órbita. El periodo inicial de trabajo se extiende desde el 4 de noviembre de 2026 hasta el 3 de mayo de 2027, con opciones para continuar hasta 2029.

Las empresas seleccionadas son Astranis Space Technologies Corp., Global Enterprise Solutions Inc. y Viasat Inc., con valores máximos de contrato de $264.3 millones, $340.4 millones y $460.9 millones, respectivamente. Este esfuerzo es parte del programa SCaN de NASA, que busca reemplazar gradualmente la flota de satélites de seguimiento y datos, adoptando servicios comerciales para futuras misiones.

La implementación de servicios en banda Ka es crucial para misiones en órbita que no pueden modificar su hardware de vuelo, asegurando así la continuidad y sostenibilidad de las comunicaciones espaciales.

article.source_body: Credit: NASA NASA selected three companies on Wednesday to perform work to develop Ka-band space relay capability concepts that are compatible with current missions in space, ensuring service continuity for existing spacecraft without requiring modifications to their onboard systems. Through this work, NASA will aim to acquire end-to-end solutions that include space, ground, launch, operations, and integration elements, as one of many customers in the commercial marketplace. The awards, under the Next Space Technologies for Exploration Partnerships-3 Broad Agency Announcement Appendix E, are firm-fixed-price contracts that give NASA the option to provide additional funding up to the award limit to advance from initial concept development and risk reduction to an in-orbit flight demonstration. The initial period of performance runs from Nov. 4 through May 3, 2027, with additional priced options to continue work through 2029. The contract awardees with maximum potential value inclusive of all future options are: Astranis Space Technologies Corp. for $264.3 million. Global Enterprise Solutions Inc. for $340.4 million. Viasat Inc. for $460.9 million. Facilitated through the agency’s SCaN (Space Communications and Navigation) program’s Communications Services Project, this work supports NASA’s decision to gradually retire the Tracking and Data Relay Satellite fleet and adopt commercial services for future missions. In addition to the commercial capabilities currently under development by the program’s industry partners, Ka-band services are needed to support select in-orbit missions that cannot feasibly modify flight hardware or transition to non-compatible commercial services. article.explanation:
**NASA cubrirá la partida de la 35.ª misión de reabastecimiento de SpaceX desde la Estación Espacial**

NASA y SpaceX están en la fase final de la 35.ª misión de reabastecimiento, con un lanzamiento programado para el 18 de noviembre. El vehículo Dragon, que transporta más de 6,300 libras de suministros y experimentos científicos, se separará de la Estación Espacial Internacional (EEI) y comenzará su regreso a la Tierra.

Entre los experimentos que regresan se encuentran un constructo de vaso sanguíneo impreso en 3D, utilizado para estudiar el envejecimiento vascular y enfermedades cardiovasculares. También se enviarán organoides tumorales tratados en la EEI, que ayudarán a los investigadores a encontrar nuevas formas de mejorar los tratamientos contra el cáncer. Además, se analizarán muestras microbianas para comprender mejor la resistencia a los antibióticos en el espacio.

El regreso del Dragon está sujeto a las condiciones meteorológicas, y se espera que el aterrizaje se realice frente a la costa de California. Aunque NASA no transmitirá el aterrizaje, proporcionará actualizaciones a través de su blog. Esta misión es parte de un esfuerzo continuo para avanzar en la investigación científica y preparar futuras misiones a la Luna y Marte.

article.source_body: A SpaceX Dragon spacecraft supporting the company’s 34th commercial resupply services mission for NASA departs the International Space Station following its undocking from the Harmony module’s forward port. Credit: NASA/Jessica Meir NASA and its international partners are set to receive scientific research samples and hardware as a SpaceX Dragon spacecraft departs the International Space Station no earlier than Wednesday, Nov. 18, for its return to Earth. Pending weather conditions, the Dragon spacecraft will undock from the Harmony module’s space-facing port at 11:05 a.m. EST, following a command sent by ground controllers at SpaceX’s facility in Hawthorne, California. NASA’s live coverage of undocking and departure begins at 10:45 a.m., streaming through a variety of platforms. Learn where to watch online: https://www.nasa.gov/live NASA and SpaceX are monitoring weather forecasts and targeting splashdown off the California coast no earlier than 1:50 a.m. Thursday, Nov. 19 (10:50 p.m. PST Nov. 18). Teams will adjust plans as needed based on splashdown conditions in the Dragon recovery area and will provide updates on splashdown timing when available. NASA will not stream the splashdown but will post updates on its space station blog . Thousands of pounds of cargo are returning from the space station, including research samples that could advance future space exploration and improve life on Earth. The returning research includes a 3D-bioprinted blood vessel construct scientists used to study vascular aging and cardiovascular disease in space and on Earth. Frozen tumor organoids treated aboard the station also will return, helping researchers identify new ways to improve cancer treatments and advance personalized medicine. Scientists will analyze frozen microbial samples to better understand how antibiotic-resistant bacteria survive, adapt, and evolve in space. In addition, a lighting system will return after more than three years aboard the space station, where researchers tested its potential to support astronauts’ sleep and well-being during long-duration missions. Filled with more than 6,300 pounds of crew supplies, science investigations, and equipment, the spacecraft arrived at the space station on Oct. 15. It launched two days earlier on a Falcon 9 rocket from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida for the agency’s SpaceX 35th commercial resupply services mission. For more than 26 years, people have lived and worked continuously aboard the International Space Station, advancing scientific knowledge and making research breakthroughs not possible on Earth. The space station helps NASA understand and overcome the challenges of human spaceflight, expand commercial opportunities in low Earth orbit, and build on the foundation for long-duration missions to the Moon, as part of the Artemis and Moon Base programs, and to Mars. **NASA lanza concurso para estudiantes sobre sistemas de energía nuclear**

NASA ha inaugurado el "Power to Explore Student Challenge", un concurso dirigido a estudiantes desde jardín infantil hasta 12° básico en Estados Unidos. Este desafío busca fomentar el aprendizaje sobre sistemas de energía nuclear en el espacio, invitando a los participantes a imaginar cómo estas "baterías" nucleares podrían impulsar la exploración lunar.

Los estudiantes deberán presentar un ensayo de 200 palabras y una ilustración original que refleje su visión de una base lunar alimentada por energía nuclear. Además, se les pide que describan un "superpoder" personal que contribuiría a la misión. Las inscripciones están abiertas hasta el 1 de marzo de 2027.

El concurso tiene como objetivo preparar a la próxima generación de exploradores para enfrentar los desafíos de la exploración lunar, especialmente en regiones con condiciones extremas. Según Carl Sandifer, gerente de programas de la División de Reactores Espaciales de NASA, la energía nuclear podría ser clave para operar en áreas permanentemente sombreadas y mantener instrumentos en funcionamiento durante las largas noches lunares.

Los ganadores de cada categoría de grado recibirán un viaje al Centro de Investigación Glenn de NASA en Cleveland, donde aprenderán sobre las tecnologías que hacen posibles las misiones espaciales.

article.source_body: The thematics for the 2026-2027 Radioisotope Power Systems Power to Explore Student Challenge Credit: NASA / David Lam NASA’s Power to Explore Student Challenge kicked off Tuesday, Nov. 17. The science, engineering, technology, and mathematics (STEM) challenge invites kindergarten through 12th grade students in the United States to learn about space nuclear power systems and illustrate how these nuclear “batteries” could help power their lunar exploration vision. Students are also invited to write a short essay about a “superpower” of their own. Submissions are due March 1, 2027. Every mission requires a power source. Some of the most interesting locations to study on our Moon face some of the harshest conditions. Nuclear power could sustain human life and allow researchers to study the resource-rich environment despite freezing temperatures, long nights, and deep craters that never see sunlight. “As NASA returns to the Moon and establishes a lunar base where astronauts will live, work, and explore, we need to build an infrastructure to make it all possible. Nuclear power could enable exploration in the permanently shadowed regions near the Moon’s South Pole, carry robust science payloads over long distances, and keep instruments warm through the lunar night,” said Carl Sandifer, a program manager for NASA’s Space Reactors Division at the agency’s headquarters in Washington. “NASA’s Power to Explore Student Challenge prepares the next generation of explorers to use the unique power within themselves to dream up a nuclear-powered Moon base of their own design. We cannot wait to see what they come up with!” Entries include a 200-word essay and an original illustration. Essays should describe one of the students’ unique powers that will help the mission. Illustrations should convey the students’ vision of a nuclear-powered lunar base that supports human and robotic exploration of the Moon’s surface using both radioisotope and fission-based power solutions and demonstrate the students’ understanding of the kinds of exploration nuclear energy can enable. Judges will review entries in three grade-level categories: K-4, 5-8, and 9-12. One grand prize winner from each grade category will receive a trip for two to NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland to learn about the people and technologies that enable NASA missions. Every student who submits an entry will receive a digital certificate and an invitation to a virtual event with NASA experts where they’ll learn about what energizes the NASA workforce to advance NASA’s missions and sustain America’s leadership in space. Judges Needed NASA and Future Engineers are seeking volunteers to help judge the thousands of contest entries anticipated from around the country. U.S. residents older than 18 who are interested in volunteering approximately three hours should register to judge at the Future Engineers website . The Power to Explore Student Challenge is funded by the NASA Science Mission Directorate and operates out of the Radioisotope Power Systems Program under the Research and Technology Mission Directorate. Future Engineers administers the challenge through a contract with the NASA Center of Excellence for Collaborative Innovation within the agency’s Research and Technology Mission Directorate. **De contratista a funcionario público: La NASA le da la bienvenida a Jim Mirandy**

Jim Mirandy, especialista en aseguramiento de calidad en el Centro Espacial Stennis de la NASA, ha hecho la transición de contratista a funcionario público. Esta decisión forma parte de una directiva de la agencia para fortalecer las competencias técnicas dentro de su personal civil. Tras 30 años como contratista, Mirandy ahora desempeña un papel crucial en la misión de la NASA de devolver a los astronautas estadounidenses a la Luna a través del programa Artemis.

Mirandy ha sido fundamental en la implementación de protocolos de seguridad y en la formación de clases de entrenamiento en alta presión y criogénico. Su experiencia específica en el centro garantiza que las pruebas de propulsión se realicen con los más altos estándares de seguridad y calidad. Además, su trabajo incluye investigar incidentes y liderar programas de protección voluntaria.

Desde su infancia en Titusville, Florida, donde su padre trabajaba en la NASA, Mirandy ha estado vinculado al mundo espacial. Su trayectoria profesional comenzó en el Michoud Assembly Facility, donde su habilidad para resolver problemas lo llevó a enfocarse en la seguridad y la calidad. Su compromiso con la mejora continua y la seguridad de sus colegas es evidente en cada aspecto de su trabajo.

article.source_body: 3 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) Jim Mirandy, quality assurance specialist at NASA’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi, poses for a photograph at the High Pressure Gas Facility on Nov. 10, 2026. Mirandy is now a NASA civil servant at Stennis as part of the administrator’s directive to strengthen technical core competencies within the civil service workforce. NASA/Danny Nowlin The rumble of a rocket engine might be considered a soundtrack for Jim Mirandy’s life. Mirandy has grown up with NASA as a constant presence, and his path to becoming a civil servant at NASA’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi, has been decades in the making. Hired under the agency’s workforce directive to restore core competencies by converting contractors to civil service, Mirandy is now a quality assurance specialist after 30 years of working as a contractor supporting NASA. “Discovery is an important job, and it is exciting to be a part of that process,” said Mirandy. “As a nation, we lead the world in space exploration, and we make that dream of reaching for the stars a reality.” His work at the nation’s largest rocket propulsion test site directly supports the agency’s mission to return American astronauts to the Moon through the Artemis program and ensure American leadership in space. By retaining Mirandy’s facility-specific expertise as a civil servant, NASA ensures that the critical propulsion testing at NASA Stennis continues to be executed with safety and quality in mind. Mirandy describes his team as an integral part of the process that provides a second set of eyes with a focus on potential hazards. As a quality assurance specialist, he serves as the agency’s close call investigator at the center, helps lead the Voluntary Protection Program, and participates in the Striving to Achieve Real Safety committee, an employee safety committee that works to keep the site safe. Mirandy also has a long resume of critical institutional contributions, including creating high pressure and cryogenic training classes that he taught for 10 years, and helping establish safety protocols throughout various locations at the center. Mirandy’s connection to America’s space agency began in childhood living in Titusville, Florida. His father, Wes Mirandy, worked for Rocketdyne at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida, and Mirandy’s nearby elementary school regularly gathered to watch launches. Later, his father worked as the A-1 test stand manager for space shuttle main engine testing at NASA Stennis. “My father was by far my greatest mentor,” said Mirandy. “My dad always included us whenever he worked on something around the house, so we picked up a knack for examining problems and fixing things. When I arrived at Stennis Space Center, many of his friends and coworkers took the time to help me succeed at my job. They took the time to explain the test stands and other systems and how they worked.” A knack for fixing things helped launch Mirandy’s career at Michoud Assembly Facility in New Orleans. He started working hands-on as a mechanic on the Space Shuttle External Tank. When an unexpected incident occurred in a production cell, Mirandy stepped up to help the operations and safety team resolve the issue. This moment shifted his career trajectory into safety and quality. Mirandy found his way to NASA Stennis and brought an understanding of systems and operations with him. A resident of Bay St. Louis and a graduate of the University of Southern Mississippi, Mirandy is motivated by helping people, keeping them safe, and improving processes. “Your reward for working safely today is tomorrow,” said Mirandy. **NASA invita a la prensa y al público a ver las primeras imágenes del telescopio Roman**

La NASA ha anunciado que el telescopio espacial Nancy Grace Roman revelará sus primeras imágenes durante una transmisión en vivo el 7 de diciembre, en el marco de la reunión anual de la Unión Geofísica Americana (AGU) en San Francisco. Este evento se llevará a cabo a las 3:30 p.m. EST y mostrará las capacidades científicas únicas del telescopio, que se propone explorar temas fundamentales como la energía oscura, la materia oscura y los exoplanetas.

Antes de la transmisión, se realizarán actividades para la prensa, incluyendo una vista previa de las imágenes a las 12 p.m. y una charla con el administrador de la NASA, Jared Isaacman, a las 2:45 p.m. Se espera que los medios registrados puedan participar en entrevistas posteriores al evento.

El telescopio Roman, lanzado el 30 de agosto, ha comenzado su viaje hacia su órbita final y está en proceso de calibración. Con su amplio campo de visión y capacidad de observación en infrarrojo, se anticipa que proporcionará datos valiosos que no solo ayudarán a entender el universo, sino que también apoyarán investigaciones en diversas áreas científicas.

article.source_body: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, seen here in the clean room at the agency’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, on Nov. 25, 2025, will explore essential questions in the areas of dark energy, exoplanets, and astrophysics. Credit: NASA/Jolearra Tshiteya NASA will release the first images from its Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope during a live stream from the American Geophysical Union (AGU) Annual Meeting in San Francisco at 3:30 p.m. EST (12:30 p.m. PST) Monday, Dec. 7. The images will showcase the unique scientific capabilities of Roman, which will soon capture deep, panoramic, never-before-seen views of the universe to explore the mysteries of dark energy, dark matter, and worlds outside our solar system. Watch the unveiling on a variety of platforms online: https://www.nasa.gov/live Roman’s first images will simultaneously post on the agency’s website . The following is a list of activities for release of the first images (all times Eastern): Dec. 7 12 p.m.: NASA will preview the images for media under embargo as part of the AGU meeting in San Francisco. To participate, either remotely or in-person, media must be registered with AGU by 8 p.m. Sunday, Dec. 6. Media can apply for AGU registration online . NASA will update this advisory later with briefing participants. The agency also will offer embargoed interviews following the conclusion of the briefing to registered media. A recording of the media briefing will be available on the AGU website after the embargo lifts at 3:30 p.m. on Dec. 7. 2:45 p.m.: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman will participate in a fireside chat at the AGU meeting, moderated by journalist Alex Witze, to discuss the powerful connections between Earth and space science, the discoveries shaping our understanding of the universe, and the role NASA science plays in advancing what is possible. 3:30 p.m.: The live broadcast for the release of Roman’s images will stream through a variety of NASA platforms, in addition to AGU channels. Tuesday, Dec. 8 6 a.m. – 1 p.m.: Roman mission experts available to conduct live, remote interviews with broadcast media. More details about scheduling these interviews are forthcoming. Pixel adoption NASA invites the public to claim a corner of the universe with one of Roman’s select first images . When Roman reveals its first images, each pixel will represent a unique piece of the cosmos. Once the image is revealed, participants can look up their personal pixel and receive a digital trading card with key information they can share with NASA social accounts. Roman community events Get involved by hosting your own event for the reveal of Roman’s first images. Roman launched Aug. 30 from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida on a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket, beginning a three-month, million-mile trip to its final orbit at the Sun-Earth Lagrange Point 2. During that journey, Roman has undergone a commissioning process where its systems are turned on, adjusted, calibrated, and prepared to conduct science. Roman will use its large field of view and crisp infrared vision to study vast swaths of the sky and probe deeply into cosmic history. In addition to helping scientists explore dark matter, dark energy, and exoplanets, Roman’s surveys will support a broad range of research extending far beyond the mission’s main science goals. The mission also will feature a cutting-edge coronagraph technology demonstration to directly image planets around other stars. The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is managed at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, with participation by NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California; Caltech/IPAC in Pasadena, California; the Space Telescope Science Institute; and a science team comprised of scientists from various research institutions. The primary industrial partners are BAE Systems, Inc.; L3Harris Technologies; and Teledyne Scientific & Imaging. NASA llevará a cabo vuelos de investigación a baja altitud sobre tierras agrícolas cercanas a Amarillo, Texas, desde el 22 de octubre hasta el 2 de noviembre de 2026. Estos vuelos utilizarán un avión Dynamic Aviation A200 para medir las emisiones gaseosas y de partículas provenientes de las operaciones de alimentación animal.

La misión, denominada FarmFlux, tiene como objetivo estudiar las emisiones agrícolas, un aspecto importante y poco investigado de los sistemas terrestres y atmosféricos de la Tierra. Durante la misión, se desplegarán más de una docena de sensores para medir contaminantes como ozono, metano, amoníaco y partículas, así como su interacción con la atmósfera.

La iniciativa es liderada conjuntamente por el Centro de Vuelo Espacial Goddard de NASA, la Universidad Estatal de Colorado y la Universidad de Boston. Además, se han programado vuelos de investigación adicionales con un avión P-3 Orion de NASA entre marzo y julio de 2027, centrados en tierras de cultivo en el Medio Oeste y el Valle Central de California. Estos esfuerzos buscan mejorar la comprensión de las emisiones agrícolas y su impacto en el medio ambiente.

article.source_body: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 18 – An… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. A Medium-Sized Solar Flare Explanation: What a flare for the chromatic ! Today’s image captures a piece of the Sun ’s chromosphere , the layer of the Sun ’s atmosphere above its surface where the temperature rises . Why would the Sun become hotter farther away from its core ? This is potentially due to energy from the swirling magnetic fields extending up through the Sun’s atmosphere. Those same magnetic fields can twist and snap , releasing light and energetic particles as a solar flare . The H-alpha filter used for today’s image captures light from energized hydrogen atoms as they travel off the Sun’s surface during a flare on May 14, 2025. This flare was classified as an M1 based on GOES observations , meaning it was moderately bright in X-rays . M-class flares can cause radio blackouts at Earth’s poles and minor radiation storms that can harm astronauts. They aren’t even the most powerful flares ! NASA, NOAA , and other agencies monitor the Sun to predict and identify such storms so we can protect humans on Earth and in space. **TITULAR: Fotos de astronautas de Gemini inspiraron programa temprano de observación de la Tierra**

En noviembre de 1966, durante la misión Gemini XII, los astronautas James Lovell y Buzz Aldrin registraron imágenes del Mar Rojo y el valle del Nilo. Este último vuelo del programa Gemini no solo cumplió objetivos técnicos espaciales, sino que demostró el valor científico de observar la superficie terrestre desde la órbita.

Las fotografías capturadas por la tripulación fueron fundamentales para que científicos e instituciones justificaran la creación de un programa satelital dedicado. William T. Pecora, entonces director del Servicio Geológico de Estados Unidos, fue un defensor clave de esta iniciativa tras notar la utilidad de los registros visuales obtenidos en las misiones Mercury y Gemini para el estudio de recursos

article.original_title: Gemini Astronaut Photos Inspired Early Earth Observation Program
article.source_body: NASA astronauts James A. Lovell Jr. and Edwin E. “Buzz” Aldrin Jr. captured this image of the area surrounding the Red Sea and Nile river valley on November 14, 1966, during their four-day mission in space. Gemini XII was the final flight of NASA’s Gemini Program. NASA Astronauts James A. Lovell Jr. and Edwin E. “Buzz” Aldrin Jr. orbited Earth from November 11 to 15, 1966, on Gemini XII , the final mission of NASA’s Gemini program. In addition to successfully completing rendezvous maneuvers and spacewalks, procedures vital to sending American astronauts to the Moon, the crew was also spurring the development of a different field of exploration, observing Earth from space. The photos taken by Lovell, Aldrin, and other Gemini astronauts demonstrated the value of orbital imagery for studying Earth’s surface. Their images helped scientists make the case for a dedicated Earth observation satellite program. One of strongest advocates for accelerating the use of Earth-observing satellites was William T. Pecora, the director of the United States Geological Survey from 1965 to 1971. In a 1969 statement, Pecora noted that the Earth Resources Observation Satellite (EROS) program he championed, and which later paved the way for Landsat , was “conceived in 1966 largely as a direct result of the demonstrated utility of Mercury and Gemini orbital photography to Earth resource studies.” For more than five decades, Landsat and other Earth-observing satellites have provided invaluable data used around the world to monitor crops, wildfires, flooding, vegetation health, land use, and countless other changes to our planet. **NASA recibe decimosexta opinión de auditoría financiera "limpia" consecutiva**

NASA ha logrado, por décimo sexta vez consecutiva, una opinión de auditoría externa "limpia" sobre sus estados financieros del año fiscal 2026. Este reconocimiento, el más alto en auditoría, asegura que los informes financieros de la agencia cumplen con los Principios de Contabilidad Generalmente Aceptados para agencias federales y reflejan con precisión su situación financiera.

El administrador de NASA, Jared Isaacman, destacó la importancia de ser responsables en la gestión de los recursos públicos y subrayó que esta auditoría limpia es un testimonio del compromiso de la agencia con la rendición de cuentas financieras. El informe financiero de 2026 también resalta los avances en las misiones de NASA, incluyendo el exitoso vuelo de prueba de la misión Artemis II, que marcó hitos significativos en la exploración espacial.

Además, se anunciaron iniciativas transformadoras para fortalecer el liderazgo estadounidense en el espacio, como la construcción de una base lunar y el lanzamiento anticipado del telescopio espacial Nancy Grace Roman, destinado a estudiar fenómenos como la materia oscura y la energía oscura. Estos logros reflejan el compromiso de NASA con la transparencia y la innovación en la exploración espacial.

article.source_body: Credit: NASA For the 16th consecutive year, NASA has received an unmodified, or “clean,” opinion from an external auditor on its fiscal year 2026 financial statements. The rating is the best possible audit opinion, certifying that NASA’s financial statements conform with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles for federal agencies and accurately present the agency’s financial position. “Our responsibility at NASA is to be disciplined stewards of the resources entrusted to us by the American people while delivering on the missions they expect from this agency,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “Our 16th consecutive clean audit reflects a long record of financial accountability, and we intend to pair that discipline with the urgency and execution required to take on the near-impossible missions ahead.” The 2026 Agency Financial Report provides key financial and performance information and demonstrates the agency’s commitment to transparency in the use of American taxpayers’ dollars. In addition, the 2026 report presents progress during the past year, and spotlights advancements in NASA missions, objectives, and workforce development with these financial resources. In fiscal year 2026 (FY 2026), NASA’s 10-day Artemis II mission successfully accomplished a test flight around the Moon with four crew members, delivering major human spaceflight milestones, such as the record‑breaking distance astronauts have traveled from Earth and global public engagement. NASA also announced a series of transformative agencywide initiatives designed to advance American leadership in space, including plans to build a Moon Base, which will be humanity’s first lunar outpost, and a place where astronauts will live, work, and explore near the Moon’s South Pole. NASA’s science advancements in FY 2026 included launching the agency’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, ahead of schedule, to study dark matter, dark energy, planets outside our solar system, as well as exploration of everything from nearby stars to distant galaxies. NASA’s experimental X-59 quiet supersonic aircraft achieved a major milestone when it flew faster than the speed of sound for the first time. The agency also: launched NASA Force with the U.S. Office of Personnel Management, a talent track designed to recruit and deploy the nation’s top engineers and technologists to support America’s space program; announced an agencywide realignment to increase mission focus; and welcomed additional Artemis Accords signatories committing to the safe, transparent, and responsible exploration of the Moon, Mars, and beyond. article.explanation: NASA ha realizado avances significativos en su experimento de navegación conocido como SPLICE (Safe and Precise Landing – Integrated Capabilities Evolution), diseñado para mejorar la precisión de los aterrizajes en la Luna y Marte. Este sistema fue probado en un dron Alta-X en el Centro de Investigación de Vuelo Armstrong en California, donde demostró su capacidad para comunicarse eficazmente durante maniobras de vuelo. El SPLICE utiliza un sistema de guía avanzado que permite mapear el terreno y evaluar áreas de aterrizaje potenciales. Si el sistema determina que el área objetivo es insegura, puede redirigir el dron a un lugar más seguro. Este enfoque es crucial para las misiones futuras de NASA, ya que garantiza aterrizajes más seguros y precisos en superficies extraterrestres. Davis Adams, gerente del proyecto, destacó que esta prueba representa el resultado de casi una década de trabajo y que el sistema está listo para ser integrado en futuras misiones robóticas y tripuladas. Además, se están realizando colaboraciones con proveedores de módulos lunares para implementar SPLICE en sus plataformas, lo que podría facilitar aterrizajes suaves en la superficie lunar en misiones venideras.

article.explanation:
**Desafío AVATAR Digital BPS**

El programa AVATAR (A Virtual Astronaut Tissue Analog Response) de la NASA se centra en el estudio de los efectos de la radiación y la microgravedad en la salud humana mediante dispositivos de organ-on-a-chip. Este experimento, que se llevará a cabo en la misión Artemis II, busca generar conocimientos que puedan beneficiar tanto a astronautas en el espacio como a la población en general.

La investigación se enmarca dentro del Programa de Biología Espacial de la NASA, que examina cómo los sistemas vivos responden a los estresores únicos de la exploración espacial. Con la mirada puesta en misiones de larga duración, se hace esencial desarrollar estrategias de salud personalizadas para proteger a los miembros de la tripulación.

El desafío digital AVATAR invita a la comunidad científica a utilizar tecnologías innovadoras de gemelos digitales para acelerar el descubrimiento biológico y modelar la salud de los astronautas. Se busca crear modelos computacionales que simulen cómo responde la médula ósea a los estresores del vuelo espacial, integrando datos diversos para generar predicciones de salud personalizadas.

Este enfoque no solo promete mejorar la salud de los astronautas, sino que también podría tener implicaciones significativas para la medicina en la Tierra.

article.source_body: 2 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) The AVATAR (A Virtual Astronaut Tissue Analog Response) investigation will use organ-on-a-chip devices, or organ chips, to study a effects of increased radiation and microgravity on human health. Artemis II AVATAR is a small experiment flying aboard Artemis II that could lead to big impacts in healthcare, both for astronauts in space and citizens on Earth. For more information on AVATAR: go.nasa.gov/4m5dGH9 The NASA Space Biology Program within the Biological and Physical Sciences (BPS) Division investigates how living systems respond across the full spectrum of biological organization to advance understanding of how living systems respond to the unique stressors of space exploration—including microgravity, ionizing radiation, low magnetic fields, and elevated CO₂. As NASA prepares for long-duration deep space missions, the need to protect individual crew members with personalized, data-driven health strategies is becoming increasingly important. The original AVATAR (A Virtual Astronaut Tissue Analog Response) investigation, which flew aboard the Artemis II mission, marks a significant milestone: organ-on-a-chip devices constructed from the cells of actual crew members returned from a 10-day lunar flyby on April 10, 2026. AVATAR is the first demonstration of an Artemis astronaut analog using an organ-on-a-chip model to generate personalized biological insights that can inform medical kits and countermeasures for future deep space missions. Digital twins represent a key strategy for addressing these challenges. By developing individualized computational physiological models that can be iteratively refined with empirical data, these frameworks integrate environmental, physiological, and multi-omics inputs. This approach allows for the simulation and prediction of how a specific individual will respond to spaceflight stressors. The BPS Digital AVATAR Challenge invites the scientific community to apply innovative computational digital twin technologies to accelerate biological discovery, biochemical and molecular modeling, and predictions of individual astronaut health outcomes. The digital twin will be a computational model of how the AVATAR bone marrow chip responds to spaceflight stressors. The proposed digital twin frameworks must be capable of processing diverse multi-modal datasets and leverage established computational biology methods alongside modern digital twin architectures to create personalized, predictive models of astronaut physiology. These systems are expected to model each astronaut’s immune and bone marrow hematopoietic responses to spaceflight, integrating multi-modal data to generate tailored health predictions — including comparative analysis that distinguishes individual-specific effects from effects common across the crew. Proposals should also demonstrate a pathway to continuous model updating as new empirical data become available, reflecting the iterative nature of a true digital twin. Entre fines de octubre y principios de noviembre de 2026, una serie de tormentas extremas azotó la región de Four Corners, en el suroeste de Estados Unidos. Este fenómeno, impulsado por temperaturas oceánicas inusualmente altas y el patrón de El Niño, provocó un aumento crítico en los caudales de la zona.

Por otro lado, los expertos documentaron el fin de la sequía de corto plazo en el suroeste y la Gran Cuenca, aunque la escasez hídrica de largo plazo aún persiste en diversos sectores del territorio.

article.source_body: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Water Surges Into Navajo… Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search September 20, 2026 November 7, 2026 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison September 20, 2026 November 7, 2026 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison September 20, 2026 November 7, 2026 Curtain Toggle 2-Up Back-to-back extreme rain events inundated the Four Corners region of the U.S. Southwest in late October and early November 2026. The storms alleviated short-term drought conditions in the Southwest but caused river levels to spike to record or near-record levels in places, triggering damaging floods. One effect of the heavy rains detected by satellites was the rapid rise of water levels in Navajo Reservoir. The change is visible in the images above, acquired on September 20 (left) and November 7 (right) with the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 . In that time, the lake in northern New Mexico and southern Colorado rose by nearly 60 feet (18 meters), according to data from the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. (Note that the Bureau of Reclamation decreased releases from Navajo Dam on September 16 and 17.) On November 7, the reservoir stood at its highest level since August 2019 and at 108 percent of the average capacity for that date. That contrasts with September 20, when it held just 60 percent of its average capacity. Due to snow drought across the West in winter 2025-26, the lake saw relatively little growth in the spring, when snowmelt often raises water levels. The San Juan, Piedra, and other rivers swelled with runoff amid the wet weather. Pagosa Springs, Colorado, a town along the San Juan River about 40 miles (64 kilometers) northeast of the lake, was especially hard-hit by flooding. In the first round of rain, 5.05 inches (12.8 centimeters) fell in the town, and on October 23 the river reached major flood stage . After more rain, the river spiked again on November 1, this time nearly to the record level set in 1911 during a devastating flood . Officials issued evacuation orders, and responders rescued dozens of people, according to news reports , while water inundated streets and damaged property. Heavy rain and flooding have been widespread across southwest Colorado, southeast Utah, northern Arizona, and northwest New Mexico in recent weeks. From early September through early November, precipitation totals were 2 to 4 times the average throughout the Four Corners region—an area beset by long-term drought that was exacerbated by snow drought and high temperatures in 2026. Though the downpours posed hazards to communities along many rivers, they did provide drought relief throughout the region. Weekly U.S. Drought Monitor maps, derived from a suite of satellite data products and ground-based observations, have indicated improvements to drought conditions due to the fall storms. The group’s November 3 summary noted that “short-term drought has ended for the Southwest and Great Basin,” although long-term drought persists in places. Wet weather in the Southwest is often associated with El Niño events, when the segment of the jet stream flowing eastward near the equatorial Pacific tends to strengthen. Experts noted that the low-pressure system delivering the heavy rainfall in autumn 2026 was at a low latitude for the time of year and drew energy from unusually high ocean temperatures. El Niño patterns—like the one currently underway —can increase the likelihood of moisture-laden storms being steered across the Southwest interior. article.explanation:
**Ecosistema oculto: Científicos descubren 245 animales viviendo dentro de una sola roca en el fondo del mar**

Investigadores han revelado un ecosistema sorprendente en el fondo del océano Pacífico, donde 245 animales habitan dentro de una única roca, conocida como nódulo polimetálico. Estos nódulos, formados por óxidos de hierro y manganeso, ofrecen refugio a organismos microscópicos en sus grietas y cavidades, creando hábitats en un entorno predominantemente blando.

El estudio, liderado por la ecóloga marina Dr. Tanja Stratmann, identificó un total de 4,139 animales en 244 nódulos, con un promedio de 17 por nódulo. Aunque la cantidad de vida en los nódulos es menor que en el sedimento circundante, su diversidad es notable. Las comunidades de animales dentro de los nódulos son genéticamente distintas de las que habitan en el sedimento, lo que sugiere que estos nódulos son hábitats especializados.

La investigación también plantea preocupaciones sobre el impacto de la minería en el fondo marino, ya que la extracción de nódulos podría llevar a la pérdida irreversible de biodiversidad. Los nódulos requieren millones de años para formarse, lo que significa que su eliminación podría resultar en la extinción de especies que dependen de estos hábitats únicos. La protección de estos ecosistemas ocultos es crucial para la conservación marina.

NGC 7129: Star Formation with Jets from Webb Explanation: How do stars form? To help answer this question, NASA used the James Webb Space Telescope to take the featured detailed image of the star-forming region NGC 7129 in infrared light . Star formation progresses when gravity pulls together massive amounts of gas, but soon things can get complicated when previously formed stars emit powerful jets and winds — and some then explode . Opaque dust can form in the cool atmospheres of stars and, when dispersed, can obstruct visible-light images. Many stars can be seen to be forming in the featured image , with the young stars on the left, in the gold-colored gas, typically being more mature than the young stars on the right — in the red region. Jets and wind s likely cause the filamentary nature of the red-colored gas. Studying stars at different stages of development bolsters understanding about what physical processes are most important and when.
